podcast.title: Early Life and Musical Upbringing
podcast.body: Born in St. Louis, Donnie Hathaway was a professional gospel singer by the age of three. He pursued music lessons and classes throughout his life, including into college, demonstrating an early and profound connection to music. "He grew up in St. Louis and was a professional gospel singer at the age of three."

podcast.title: Gospel vs. Pop Dilemma
podcast.body: Throughout his career, Hathaway struggled to reconcile his deeply gospel-oriented background, as noted by his high school band director, with the demands of making pop music. This internal conflict led him to consistently include at least one gospel song on his records. "He had a really hard time reconciling making pop music instead of gospel. So he always included a gospel song on his records."

podcast.title: Howard University Scholarship
podcast.body: In the fall of 1963, Hathaway enrolled in classes at Howard University, having received a fine art scholarship primarily due to his exceptional piano skills. Initially, he considered paths like teaching or preaching, but music was ingrained in his DNA. "In the fall of 1963, he enrolled in classes at Howard University, thanks in part to a fine art scholarship because of his piano skills."

podcast.title: Live Performance Style
podcast.body: Like a true jazz musician, Donnie Hathaway possessed a seemingly innate ability to make each live performance a unique experience. David Ritz, author of a short book about "Donnie Hathaway Live," emphasized that the live Donnie was the most moving, unadorned, and direct representation of his artistry. "Like a true jazz musician, he had this seemingly innate ability to make each live performance, a new performance."

podcast.title: Producer and Arranger Work
podcast.body: In the late 1960s, before launching his solo recording career, Hathaway worked extensively as a producer and arranger for prominent artists such as The Staple Singers and Aretha Franklin. "In the late 1960s, Hathaway worked as a producer and an arranger for the likes of the staple singers and Rita Franklin."
